intervals.label: Tunka-133 operation
intervals.note: The April 2021 arXiv text says the array "is taking data since 2009"; the TAIGA collaboration's 2022 overview says "in 2012 we finished deployment of the Tunka-133 array" (six satellite clusters were added in 2011). No later statement that the array is still running was read, so "active" with an open end is the last reported state.

placements.quote: in the Tunka valley 50 km to the west from Lake Baikal (51.49 N, 103.04 E)

altitude.quote: The Tunka-133 array is located at an altitude of 670 m a.s.l.

area.quote: arranged over an area of 3 km2

energy_range.quote: in the energy range from 6 · 1015 to 1018 eV

summary.plain: 175 light detectors in 25 clusters that record the blue Cherenkov flash of cosmic-ray air showers on dark nights.
summary.technical: Tunka-133: 175 optical detectors in 25 hexagonal clusters (six plus one central) over about 3 km2 at 670 m; PMT-based Cherenkov-light lateral-distribution measurement; winter-season operation.

technology.quote: The detectors are grouped into 25 clusters with seven detectors each
technology.value: Array of 175 photomultiplier-based optical detectors (in 25 clusters of seven) measuring the Cherenkov light of air showers at night.
